description: We are a six-member team from MANIT Bhopal building Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map, an interactive 3D Mars globe for future off-world exploration. Combining Akshat’s planetary research and Rishabh’s data analysis, we turn complex Martian datasets into survival insights—powered by a backend engineered by Sameer and Mohammed, and visualized through a 3D interface built by Anas and Muskhan.
summary:
MIRA: Martian Interactive Rendering Atlas

Imagine standing on Mars, preparing for your next exploration mission. You know your destination, but do you understand the terrain, the elevation changes, the scientific significance of the route, or the challenges that lie ahead?

MIRA transforms fragmented planetary datasets into an intuitive exploration experience. Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, MIRA combines real Martian data, interactive 3D visualization, intelligent route planning, and AI-powered guidance into a single platform. Using datasets such as NASA Mars Trek, MOLA elevation data, and planetary science repositories, users can explore Mars, inspect terrain, analyze elevation profiles, and discover scientifically important locations.

What makes MIRA unique is its focus on journey-based exploration rather than simple map visualization. Instead of only showing where a location exists, MIRA helps users understand what lies between their starting point and destination. Through terrain-aware route planning powered by pathfinding algorithms and the MIRA AI Copilot, users gain contextual insights into the Martian environment and potential exploration paths.

Our vision is to evolve MIRA into a future mission-support platform that can assist astronauts with route assessment, terrain awareness, scientific exploration, and informed decision-making, bringing humanity one step closer to meaningful exploration of Mars.
details:
1. FRONTEND RUNTIME LIBRARIES

1. React (v19.3.1)

Purpose: Builds MIRA's user interface using reusable components, hooks and state management.

2. React DOM (v19.3.1)

Purpose: Renders React components into the website's HTML document.

3. CesiumJS – cesium (v1.147.0)

Purpose: Powers MIRA's interactive 3D Mars globe, camera controls, planetary ellipsoid, terrain and satellite imagery layers.

4. Three.js – three (v0.187.0)

Purpose: Creates the 3D Solar System, planetary bodies, lighting, textures, orbital visualisation and animations.

5. Lucide React – lucide-react (v1.68.0)

Purpose: Provides icons for buttons, navigation menus, scientific panels and other interface elements.

Additional Three.js module:

- OrbitControls.js

Purpose: Provides interactive camera rotation, zooming and navigation around the 3D Solar System. It is part of Three.js, not a separate installed library.

2. FRONTEND DEVELOPMENT AND BUILD TOOLS

6. Vite – vite (v8.3.5)

Purpose: Runs MIRA's development server, builds production files and provides a preview server.

7. TypeScript – typescript (v7.0.2)

Purpose: Adds static typing to JavaScript and helps identify coding errors before execution.

8. @vitejs/plugin-react (v6.2.1)

Purpose: Integrates React and its JSX transformation and Fast Refresh functionality with Vite.

9. vite-plugin-cesium (v1.2.23)

Purpose: Configures Cesium's assets, workers and static resources during the Vite build.

10. Tailwind CSS – tailwindcss (v4.3.4)

Purpose: Provides utility-based CSS styling for MIRA's user interface.

11. @tailwindcss/vite (v4.3.4)

Purpose: Integrates Tailwind CSS processing directly into Vite.

3. TYPESCRIPT DECLARATION LIBRARIES

12. @types/react (v19.3.0)

Purpose: Provides TypeScript definitions for React components, hooks and properties.

13. @types/react-dom (v19.3.0)

Purpose: Provides TypeScript definitions for React DOM operations.

14. @types/three (v0.187.0)

Purpose: Provides TypeScript definitions for Three.js classes, objects and methods.

4. PYTHON BACKEND LIBRARIES

15. FastAPI (>=0.115.0)

Purpose: Creates MIRA's backend API endpoints for AI Copilot, elevation queries, orbital calculations and health checks.

16. Uvicorn (uvicorn[standard]) (>=0.30.0)

Purpose: Runs MIRA's Python backend as an ASGI web server.

17. HTTPX – httpx (>=0.27.0)

Purpose: Makes asynchronous HTTP requests to external services such as NASA JPL Horizons, USGS elevation services and Google's Gemini API.

18. Pydantic – pydantic (>=2.8.0)

Purpose: Validates API requests and responses and defines structured data models.

5. ADDITIONAL PYTHON PACKAGES DECLARED

19. pydantic-settings (>=2.4.0)

Purpose: Provides settings management using environment variables. Listed as a dependency, but no direct active usage was identified.

20. python-dotenv (>=1.0.0)

Purpose: Loads environment variables from .env files. Listed as a dependency, but MIRA currently implements its own .env loader.

21. NumPy – numpy (>=1.26.0)

Purpose: Provides numerical arrays and mathematical operations. Listed as a dependency, but no direct NumPy import was identified.

22. pytest (>=8.0.0)

Purpose: Python testing framework. Listed as a dependency, while the supplied backend tests use unittest.

23. pytest-asyncio (>=0.23.0)

Purpose: Provides asynchronous testing support for pytest. Listed as a dependency, but no direct current usage was identified.

6. PYTHON STANDARD LIBRARIES

These are built into Python and do not require separate installation.

24. math

Purpose: Performs mathematical calculations for planetary orbits.

25. datetime

Purpose: Handles dates and time calculations for astronomical ephemerides.

26. time

Purpose: Handles time-based operations and caching.

27. re

Purpose: Performs text processing and pattern matching.

28. uuid

Purpose: Generates unique identifiers.

29. struct

Purpose: Reads and processes binary elevation data.

30. os

Purpose: Handles environment variables and operating-system operations.

31. pathlib

Purpose: Manages file and directory paths.

32. typing

Purpose: Provides type hints for Python fu
